name: Kitsuvo — AI site filter
short_description: Local AI-builder evidence and optional search filtering.
description:
Less AI in search. Kitsuvo can hide AI answers and likely AI-built results on Google.com, Bing and DuckDuckGo, and it shows the local builder evidence for the page you are on. Both search settings are optional and off by default. Your browser. Your choice.

Hide AI answers in search (optional, off by default): when you turn it on, Kitsuvo hides the search engine's own AI answer panels, such as Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, Bing Copilot answers and Duck.ai, along with the engine's links into its AI chat. It reads the search page only; nothing is clicked, fetched or sent. When an answer is hidden, a banner on the page says so, and Show AI answer brings it back on that page. Turn the setting off to show everything again.

Filter likely AI-builder search results (optional, off by default): when you turn it on, Kitsuvo hides results hosted on known AI-builder domains. Only strong hosting signals count; weaker hosting is not hidden on hosting alone. It checks each result's link and never opens a result in the background. Show hidden results reveals them on the page. After a scan, Always show this host in search keeps that exact host visible.

Show Kitsuvo status on search pages (on by default while a search setting is on; untick it in the popup to turn it off): a short line above the results says what Kitsuvo checked or hid on that search. When results are hidden, Wrong verdict? lists their hosts, and Always show keeps an exact host visible on this device. How this works opens kitsuvo.com/extensions. Hide this line turns the line off, and the popup checkbox brings it back. It reads the search page only and sends nothing.

The search settings ask for access only to the supported Google.com, Bing and DuckDuckGo search pages, and only when you turn one on. That access is removed when both are off. Also on Google (localized) (optional, off by default, shown while a search setting is on) extends both settings to Google's country sites, such as google.de, google.co.jp and google.com.br. It asks for access to those country search pages only when you tick it, and that access is removed when you untick it or turn both search settings off. Search engines change their pages; anything Kitsuvo does not recognize stays visible.

Scan this page: Kitsuvo checks the current page for known AI-builder fingerprints, generator tags and builder hosting, then shows the score, suspected builder and each observation. It reads the page only after you press the button.

Block known AI-builder sites (Chrome, Edge and other Chromium browsers only; optional, off by default): stops top-level visits to known AI-builder hosting domains before they load. It asks for the blocking permission when you turn it on and releases it when you turn it off. It does not block custom domains based on a scan. To visit a blocked site, turn the switch off and reload.

The popup also includes Page ruler, which shows element sizes, spacing and computed CSS on the current page and can preview style or text changes until the page reloads. It runs only when you press it.

No account, API key, cloud model, telemetry, browsing-history database, or desktop companion is needed. Sign-in provider pages, password-field pages, and private tabs are skipped. Page content is not uploaded. Settings stay in local extension storage.

AI-built is provenance, not proof of harm. A low score does not prove human authorship or safety. This extension uses a focused local fingerprint subset of Kitsuvo's desktop detector. It does not provide the desktop browser's slop or impersonation checks, cloud verdicts, or page-analysis navigation gates.
single_purpose: Less AI in search. Kitsuvo hides AI answers and likely AI-built sites in Google.com, Bing and DuckDuckGo results, and shows the local AI-builder evidence for the current page so the user can see why a site counts as likely AI-built. Each hiding setting is optional, off by default and reversible.

permission_justifications.activeTab: Read the current tab only after the user presses Scan this page or Page ruler in the popup. No other tab is read.
permission_justifications.scripting: Run the bundled local detector or Page ruler in the current tab after the user presses its button, and register the search-page script on the supported search pages when the user turns on Hide AI answers in search or Filter likely AI-builder search results.
permission_justifications.storage: Save six settings and one rating counter locally on this device: searchFilter (search-result filter on or off), hideAiPanels (Hide AI answers in search on or off), navigationBlock (Chromium-only Block known AI-builder sites on or off), alwaysShowHosts (exact hostnames the user chose to always show in filtered results, from the popup or from Wrong verdict? on a search page), searchStatus (whether the short status line shows on search pages), tourVersion (the guide version the user completed or closed) and rateAsk (a capped count of results the search filter hid, up to 5, and of the days it hid one, up to 3, the last such date, and the user's Rate, Not now or Don't ask again choice, used only to decide when the popup offers a store rating link). Page content, scan reports, paths, query strings and browsing history are not stored.
permission_justifications.optional_host_permissions: Requested only when the user turns on Hide AI answers in search or Filter likely AI-builder search results, and only for the Google.com, Bing and DuckDuckGo search pages. The search-page script reads those pages to hide AI answer panels or results hosted on known AI-builder domains, and adds a banner with Show AI answer and Show hidden results, plus a short status line the user can hide. The access is removed when both settings are off. The Google country search pages (for example www.google.de/search and www.google.co.jp/search) are a separate optional grant, requested only when the user ticks Also on Google (localized) and removed when it is unticked or both settings are off. No other site receives persistent access.
permission_justifications.declarativeNetRequest: Optional, Chromium builds only. Requested only when the user turns on Block known AI-builder sites. One dynamic rule blocks top-level HTTP(S) navigation to the reviewed list of known AI-builder hosting domains. It does not read request content, block subresources or embedded frames, or redirect. The permission is released when the user turns the switch off.

data_collection: None. The extension collects and transmits no user data and loads no remote code. Page scans and search-page changes run locally, and settings stay in local extension storage.
reviewer_instructions: No account or credentials are required. 1. Open https://example.com, open the Kitsuvo popup and press Scan this page to see the local report. 2. Turn on Hide AI answers in search and accept the prompt for access to the supported search sites. On a Google.com, Bing or DuckDuckGo search that shows an AI answer panel, the panel is hidden and a banner offers Show AI answer. Whether an engine shows an AI answer depends on the query and region. 3. Turn on Filter likely AI-builder search results. Results hosted on known AI-builder domains, such as lovable.app sites, are hidden, and Show hidden results restores them. 4. With a search setting on, a short status line appears above the results. With nothing hidden it says how many results were checked; with results hidden, Wrong verdict? lists their hosts, each with Always show. Hide this line removes the line, and Show Kitsuvo status on search pages in the popup brings it back. 5. With a search setting on, tick Also on Google (localized) and accept the prompt for the Google country search pages; the same settings then work on, for example, google.de and google.co.jp. Untick it to remove that access. 6. Turn both search settings off. The optional search-site access is removed and hidden items return. 7. Chromium builds only: turn on Block known AI-builder sites and accept the blocking permission. Top-level visits to known AI-builder hosting domains are blocked; turn the switch off and reload to visit. Firefox and Safari builds do not show this switch. 8. Page ruler opens an on-page inspector on the current tab; Esc closes it. Browser settings pages, sign-in providers, password-field pages and private tabs return a skipped status. Built-in Help replays the optional guide. Use the readable source archive and tests for controlled fingerprint fixtures.
